# Adaeze Hassan

Oulu, Finland | adaeze.hassan@mail.example

## Education

MSc Environmental Engineering, Oulujoki University, 2001

## Professional Experience

**Signal Processing Engineer** — Hohtola Photonics, Oulu
2002 – present

- Designed and implemented the real-time embedded signal-conditioning pipeline for the LP-400 optical sensor product line. All processing firmware written in C++ targeting TI C6000 DSP processors under hard 50 µs cycle-time constraints; the pipeline has shipped in every LP-400 variant since 2007.
- Primary technical liaison with international partners and customers. All internal documentation, design specifications, and test protocols written in English; English is the team's working language for all design reviews and external communication.
- Based at Hohtola Photonics' Oulu headquarters since 2002. The entire sensor R&D division works onsite.

## Selected Projects

**Hohtola Internal Calibration Toolkit (HICT)** — Python, 2015 – present
Built and maintained the calibration-data processing pipeline used across the sensor validation team for production-line QA. Grew from a personal utility into a CI-integrated package (v4.2), unit-tested with pytest, used daily by eight engineers on two product lines. Written and maintained as production Python — not one-off analysis scripting.

**LP-600 Antenna Feed Characterisation Campaign** — 2018–2019
Led the antenna-feed element characterisation for the LP-600 aperture assembly. Measured S-parameters and radiation patterns with a Keysight PNA-X vector network analyser and the Oulujoki University anechoic chamber across 8–12 GHz, comparing measured element patterns against HFSS simulation models. Results informed a feed-network redesign that improved sidelobe performance by 2.3 dB.

**Publications and Open Source**
Co-authored "Wideband element-pattern calibration for sparse aperture arrays," Proc. Baltic Microwave Conference, 2019. Maintainer of aperture-utils, an open-source Python library for aperture-illumination analysis (~120 stars on GitHub).

**EU Kestrel 2020 — RADSAT Consortium** — 2020–2023
Contributed to Work Package 3 (sensor front-end validation) of the EU-funded RADSAT collaborative project as a Hohtola representative. Consortium participation terms required EU work authorisation, held as a Finnish citizen.

## Technical Skills

C++ (embedded, real-time) · Python (NumPy, SciPy, pytest, CI pipelines) · MATLAB · VHDL (basic FPGA prototyping) · VNA operation and anechoic-chamber measurement · Optical sensor calibration · Git, Jenkins CI

## Languages

Finnish (native), English (working language), Igbo (conversational)
application.cover_letter_markdown:
Dear Hiring Team,

In twenty-two years at Hohtola Photonics I have shipped embedded firmware, written production-grade tooling, and measured antenna patterns in the chamber — all on the same product line, and all from Oulu. When I saw the Senior Signal Processing Engineer role at Kaikuvaara, what caught my attention was not the job title but the work itself: the signal processing at the core of your instruments is the technical direction I have been wanting to move in.

The closest my career has come to your core discipline was a 2018–2019 project characterising the 16-element feed array in Hohtola's LP-600 aperture module. I implemented the near-field-to-far-field transform for the element array pattern, validated beamforming weight sets against measured data across the full 8–12 GHz operating band, and iterated the weight optimisation in Python before committing the production version to the embedded C++ firmware. Working through phased-array signal processing end to end — from algorithm design through to deployed code, and seeing sidelobe performance improve by 2.3 dB when the array went back into the chamber — is what convinced me that array-level signal processing is where I want to build the next stage of my career.

Beyond that project, what I would bring to Kaikuvaara is a track record of things that ship and stay shipped. The LP-400 embedded DSP pipeline I wrote has been in continuous production since 2007 without a fundamental rewrite — it processes sensor data for three product variants, and the firmware runs on every unit that has left the factory in the past nineteen years. The internal calibration toolkit I built for my own use grew into an eight-engineer daily-driver Python package with full test coverage and CI integration. When I take something on, I deliver it to a standard where other engineers can depend on it, and I follow through on the maintenance for as long as the tool is in use.

I also have experience leading small project teams through delivery-critical phases. At this point in my career I am looking for deeper technical scope in array signal processing rather than a management track, but I am comfortable taking on leadership responsibilities when the project needs it.

Practically, Oulu is home — I have lived and worked here since 2002, I know the local engineering community through the university's microwave-group seminars and the annual Polar Engineering workshop, and I have no intention of leaving. I would bring stability, deep familiarity with Oulu's engineering ecosystem, and the working habits of someone who has built and maintained systems here for over two decades.

I would welcome the chance to discuss the role and how my background fits it. I am available at your convenience.

Yours faithfully,
Adaeze Hassan

extraction_contract.task: You are the extraction step of a candidate-screening support tool. For the one candidate in this task, read the CV and cover letter in full and classify, for EACH of the 12 requirements listed, exactly one status from this fixed vocabulary: evidence_found, claim_only, contradiction, not_stated. This is extraction, not evaluation -- you are locating and quoting what the text says, never judging whether the candidate is good enough.

status_definitions.evidence_found: The text gives a concrete, specific example of the requirement (a named project, employer, tool, or role detail) -- not just a keyword or a bare assertion.
status_definitions.claim_only: The requirement is asserted (e.g. listed as a skill, or claimed in a sentence) but with no concrete project, employer, or detail backing it up.
status_definitions.contradiction: Two statements in the application -- CV vs CV, letter vs letter, or CV vs letter -- cannot both be true at once about this requirement (e.g. a degree conferral date that is later than a job that required the degree; a claimed leadership title alongside a work-history entry that describes an individual-contributor role for the same employer and period). Quote both conflicting statements. Do not decide which statement is correct or resolve the conflict -- record that it exists.
status_definitions.not_stated: The text does not explicitly and unambiguously address the requirement, under any name for it, canonical or otherwise.

extraction_contract.refuse_to_guess_rule: REFUSE TO GUESS. If the requirement is not explicitly and unambiguously addressed in the text, the status is not_stated -- full stop. Never infer a requirement from a related or similar-sounding skill, a job title alone, general seniority, years of experience, or the prestige of an employer or university. A candidate whose job title was 'Senior RF Engineer' has NOT thereby evidenced hands-on RF measurement work unless the text itself describes that work. Where the text describes substantive work in different words from the requirement's own name, quote what the text actually says and let the quoted substance speak; what a description in adjacent vocabulary amounts to is a judgement call for the human recruiter, not something this extraction step resolves by guessing in either direction. When genuinely unsure between two statuses, choose the more conservative one (not_stated over claim_only, claim_only over evidence_found) and say so in the line's note.
extraction_contract.no_verdict_rule: This tool never ranks, scores, shortlists, rejects, or recommends a candidate, and never characterises the candidate as a whole. Do not use words or phrases like recommend, reject, shortlist, rank, top candidate, best, worst, strong candidate, weak candidate, good fit, poor fit, hire, do not hire, suitable, unsuitable, pass, advance, or any other language that compares this candidate to others or states what should happen to their application. State only what the text shows, per requirement. The recruiter decides; this output is preparation, not a decision.
extraction_contract.citation_rule: Every evidence_found, claim_only, or contradiction line must carry a VERBATIM quote: copied character-for-character from the CV or cover letter text given to you (leading/trailing whitespace may be trimmed, but do not paraphrase, summarise, correct, translate, or combine separate sentences). Tag every quote with its source: 'cv' or 'cover_letter'. A quote that cannot be found verbatim in the source document will fail citation verification and be reported as invented evidence -- when in doubt, quote a shorter, exact fragment rather than a paraphrase.
extraction_contract.ask_in_screening_rule: For EVERY must-have requirement (category 'must_have') whose status you set to not_stated, add one entry to the top-level ask_in_screening list: a plain, neutral, single-sentence question the recruiter could ask in a screening call to find out. Do not add ask_in_screening entries for desirable or constraint requirements, and do not add one for a must-have that is not not_stated. Questions must be neutral fact-finding, never leading and never implying a verdict (e.g. 'Can you describe your hands-on RF measurement experience, if any?' -- not 'Do you actually have RF experience, since your CV doesn't show it?').

return_format.description: Return a single JSON object for this one candidate (when extraction runs in a batch of 8, return a JSON array of 8 such objects, one per candidate, in the same order as the batch's `tasks` list).

schema.candidate_id: string, must match the task's candidate_id

requirements.status: one of: evidence_found, claim_only, contradiction, not_stated

lines.quote: verbatim quote from the application text (see citation_rule)

requirements.note: string or null -- required and must explain the conflict without resolving it when status is 'contradiction'; optional free-text otherwise (e.g. to flag a conservative-status judgement call under refuse_to_guess_rule)

return_format.note: The `requirements` array must contain exactly one entry per requirement given in this task, in the same order, covering all 12 requirement ids.
